title: VLAN Configuration, Part 3: Inter-VLAN Routing
labSub: Let different VLANs talk to each other

scenes.narration: So far, each V L A N is a sealed floor. PC one can't reach PC two, and that's by design. Now we'll build the elevator. Here's the plan. First, you'll see why V L A Ns need a router to talk. Then you'll build the classic router on a stick. You'll prove it with a ping between two different V L A Ns. And finally, you'll do the same job faster, on a layer three switch.

items.t: Understand why VLANs need a router
Prove it with a ping across VLANs
Do the same job on a Layer 3 switch

scenes.heading: Floors and an elevator
scenes.narration: Each floor is a V L A N, and people can move around freely inside their own floor. To visit another floor, they need an elevator. Router on a stick is one elevator with a single door onto the shared corridor. A layer three switch is a whole bank of fast elevators built into the building.

items.real: A router, or a layer 3 switch

scenes.narration: First, the switch side. The port facing the router must be a trunk. On SW one, we select the port that connects to R one. And we make it a trunk, so it can carry both V L A Ns.

steps.note: A trunk carries VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 together.

scenes.narration: Now the router. One physical port will act as two gateways, using sub interfaces. We bring the physical port up, with no shutdown. It needs no address of its own. Then we create a sub interface for V L A N ten. We tell it to read the V L A N ten tag, using encapsulation dot one Q ten. And we give it the gateway address for that network. The same again for V L A N twenty, with its own address.

steps.note: Turn the port on. No IP here.
A sub-interface is a virtual door.
Match this sub-interface to VLAN 10 tags.
This becomes PC1 and PC3's gateway.

scenes.narration: Let's check that the router sees both networks. Show I P interface brief lists the two sub interfaces, both up. And show I P route has both networks as directly connected. Now the proof. PC one pings PC two, which is in a completely different V L A N. It works. And notice the T T L is one twenty seven, one less than normal. That's the router in the middle.

out: Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status      Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0     unassigned      YES unset  up          up

steps.note: The router now knows both networks.
Different VLAN. This only works with routing.
TTL dropped by 1: one router hop.

scenes.heading: Two ways to route
scenes.narration: Here's how the two designs compare. Router on a stick uses one cable and sub interfaces. A layer three switch uses virtual interfaces, called S V Is, inside the switch itself. One uses a trunk, and the other needs no cable at all. The router link can bottleneck, but the switch routes at hardware speed. So use router on a stick for small sites, and a layer three switch for anything bigger.

Now the layer three switch version. This is a Catalyst 3560, and routing is off by default. First we turn routing on, with I P routing. Then we create an S V I for V L A N ten, and give it the gateway address. And the same for V L A N twenty. Show I P interface brief shows both S V Is up. They only come up when a port in that V L A N is active. And show I P route has the two connected networks, with no router at all.

steps.note: Without this, the switch only switches.
An SVI is the VLAN's virtual gateway.
SVIs need an active port in their VLAN.

lines.c: show ip interface brief | include Vlan

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three inter-VLAN routing traps. The switch port facing the router must be a trunk. Each sub interface needs its encapsulation line before the address. And a layer three switch will not route until you type I P routing.

items.right: The router port needs a trunk on the switch
Each sub-interface needs encapsulation dot1Q first
A Layer 3 switch won't route until you enable it

scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva inter-VLAN routing lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Different V L A Ns need a router, or a layer three switch. Router on a stick uses sub interfaces with encapsulation dot one Q. A layer three switch uses S V Is, after I P routing. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva inter-VLAN routing lab.

points.t: Different VLANs need a router or L3 switch
Router on a stick: subinterfaces + dot1Q
